text: Ticket INC-88120: user U-1042 called, says she is locked out and wants her password reset. Please handle it.

result.title: Runbook: Password reset for a locked account
result.text: Runbook: Password reset for a locked account. Step 1: Verify the caller's identity using two pieces of information from the HR record - never accept a manager's word alone. Step 2: Confirm the account is locked rather than disabled; a disabled account indicates a leaver process and must not be re-enabled by the Service Desk. Step 3: Unlock the account in the directory console. Step 4: Reset the password only if the user cannot recall it; an unlock alone is sufficient after repeated failed logins. Step 5: Set the must-change-at-next-logon flag. Step 6: Record the verification method used in the ticket. Escalate to Identity Services if the account locks again within one hour, which indicates a cached credential on another device.

result.title: Runbook: Offboarding a leaver
result.text: Runbook: Offboarding a leaver. Step 1: Disable the account on the leaving date, do not delete it. Step 2: Convert the mailbox to shared and grant the manager access for ninety days. Step 3: Revoke all active sessions and reset the password to a random value. Step 4: Reclaim licences after the mailbox conversion, not before, or the mailbox becomes inaccessible. Step 5: Collect the device and confirm the encryption key is still escrowed before re-imaging. Step 6: Transfer OneDrive content to the manager. Step 7: Retain the disabled account for ninety days before deletion. Any deviation requires HR approval recorded in the ticket.

result.title: Disk encryption recovery key not found
result.text: Disk encryption recovery key not found. Recovery keys are escrowed to the device record in the management console at the point of encryption. A device with no key present was almost certainly encrypted before enrolment or was re-imaged without re-enrolling. Check the previous device record before concluding the key is lost. If no key exists anywhere, the data is unrecoverable and the device must be re-imaged; there is no vendor backdoor and no escalation path that recovers it. This is the reason the pre-enrolment encryption check exists in the build process and must not be skipped.
